title: The 'virtual DOM' is a tree of elements

slides.say: You will hear the term virtual DOM a lot. The new react dot dev docs do not use it. Here is what people mean.
Your components return React elements: plain JavaScript objects describing the UI. A tree of them lives in memory. That is the popular virtual DOM.

slides.text: React compares the new tree with the old one and syncs the real DOM. That’s reconciliation.
slides.say: On each update, React compares the new element tree with the previous one, and syncs the real DOM to match. That process is called reconciliation.

slides.text: Not the Shadow DOM. Internally React also keeps "fibers". (Simplified.)
slides.say: It is not the Shadow DOM, which is a browser feature. And internally, React also keeps objects called fibers. This is a simplified picture.
